subject: Inconsistent error messages when fitting models

messages.author: 6d3a2e43d93989dc
messages.subject: Inconsistent error messages when fitting models
parts:
Hi,  I hope this isn’t too basic of a question.  I’m mostly a beginner in R, and so far have been able to answer my own questions/troubleshoot based on previously answered questions.

 

I have count data for several species from dependent double observer surveys.  It’s a small dataset since it was for a sideproject.  I was able to get everything to work when fitting models for the counts of all species combined, but when I try to do the same for just one species at a time, I keep getting error messages like this:

 

Error in optim(starts, nll, method = method, hessian = se, ...) :

  non-finite finite-difference value [6]

 

Warning message:
In gmultmix(~1, ~1, ~observer - 1 + Date + Start_Time + Time_Elapsed +  :
  Hessian is singular. Try using fewer covariates.

 

The one exception is when I run the script for the species with the most observations – all models worked for it.  The same covariates are being used for all species combined and for each separately.  Is it likely that the R script is fine, but that I simply don’t have enough observations/data for most species for this type of analysis to be appropriate?  (there were a total of 118 observations, and the observations for each species ranged from 1-55)

 

Thank you!  Part of my script is below:  (I left out the parts that were just formating the data to fit in the unmarkedFrame, and only included a few models)

 

observer <- read.csv("Obs ID2.csv")[1:3,]

observer

obsToY <- matrix(1, 2, 2)

numPrimary <- 6

obsToY <- kronecker(diag(numPrimary), obsToY)

 

depDoubPiFun <- function(p) {

  M <- nrow(p)

  pi <- matrix(NA, M, 2)

  pi[,1] <- p[,1]

  pi[,2] <- p[,2]*(1-p[,1])

  return(pi)

}

 

all_species_umf <- unmarkedFrameGMM(y, siteCovs = NULL,

obsCovs = list(observer = observer, Date = Date_df, Start_Time = Start_Time_df, Time_Elapsed = Time_Elapsed_df,

                Ave_Temp = Ave_Temp_df, Cloud = Cloud_df, Distance = Distance_df),

          numPrimary=numPrimary, obsToY=obsToY, piFun="depDoubPiFun")

 

null <- gmultmix(~1, ~1, ~observer-1, data = all_species_umf, mixture = "NB", K=150)

 

m_DA <- gmultmix(~1, ~1, ~observer-1 + Date, data = all_species_umf, mixture = "NB", K=150)

 

DA_TE <- gmultmix(~1, ~1, ~observer-1 + Date+Time_Elapsed, data = all_species_umf, mixture = "NB", K=150)

 

All <- gmultmix(~1, ~1, ~observer-1 + Time_Elapsed + Start_Time + Ave_Temp + Cloud + Distance + Date, data = all_species_umf, mixture = "NB", K=150)

 

 

(I realize this is getting pretty complex, but when I get errors, it’s often with simpler models with only one covariate, as well as with the complex ones)

messages.subject: Re: Inconsistent error messages when fitting models
parts:
Hi Erica,

Providing starting values can sometimes help with the Hessian issue, but sparse data can also cause problems with optimization.   For any species with only a handful of non-zero observations, I think you're kind of out of luck.  If I'm doing my math correct, here, you have about 20 sites by 6 visits?


Cheers,

John

messages.subject: Re: Inconsistent error messages when fitting models
parts:
I forgot to say that earlier in my work with this data (using a different model), I had gotten the Hessian message and fixed it by providing starting values as suggested, but that it did not correct the problem this time.  So it's probably the sparse data?  I actually only have 3 sites by 6 visits:  the 118 was the total number of times animals were observed. 

I tried lumping the observations from the two observers into one value for each survey, and analyzing it with a N-mixture model (pcount), and the results were somewhat better.  I think that is appropriate, since the question I am asking is about relative abundance, rather than a precise census of each species? 

Thanks for your help!

messages.author: 4a635fe980c8c1cd
messages.subject: Re: Inconsistent error messages when fitting models
parts:
Hi Erica, thanks for the further information. Scattered thoughts:
  • The design fits gmultmix, but with very few observations for some species, I think phi and p may be pretty difficult to disentangle.  Maybe less important for fitting but something to think about: N (or the superpopulation M, in gmultmix) is assumed to have some parametric distribution, but 3 spatial replicates may make it challenging to find a reasonable parameter.
  • Don't suggest pooling the observer counts into 1 value unless the birds seen by each observer are mutually exclusive: double-counting, etc. You could pick one observers observations, I guess.
  • Since primary interest seems to be p, might be worthwhile to ditch the extra hierarchical level associated with gmultmix, stack site-visits combinations, and use multinomPois.  Main conceptual difference is that abundance is no longer thought of as a sort of super-population (the birds that might have been present over the duration of the survey) and instead the number of birds that might be possible to detect during a single visit.  The information used to estimate p remains the same, but you won't have availability getting in the way of things.
  • If one really needed to try to figure out causes of detection variance for all of these species, BUGS/JAGS will probably at least converge even for the smallest sample size, and maybe an approach conditioning N out of the likelihood would, too. I don't really know exactly at which # of observations optimization is likely to start crashing and burning.
Cheers,

John
